content: The protein known as ATP-binding cassette sub-family G member 5 (ABCG5) is encoded by the ABCG5 gene in humans. The protein encoded by this gene belongs to the superfamily of ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. ABC transporters are responsible for the translocation of various molecules across both extracellular and intracellular membranes. The ABC gene family is categorized into seven distinct subfamilies: ABC1, MDR/TAP, MRP, ALD, OABP, GCN20, and White. The ABCG5 protein is a member of the White subfamily. This protein functions as a half-transporter, playing a critical role in limiting the absorption of sterols in the intestine and facilitating their excretion via bile. Its expression is tissue-specific, predominantly occurring in the liver, colon, and intestine. The ABCG5 gene is arranged in tandem on chromosome 2, positioned in a head-to-head orientation with its family member, ABCG8. Mutations in the ABCG5 gene have been implicated in the pathological accumulation of sterols, which can contribute to the development of atherosclerosis. Such mutations have also been observed in individuals diagnosed with sitosterolemia, a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by the accumulation of plant sterols in the body.
